plain_english_title: How VA Scar and Disfigurement Rules Changed in 2002, 2008, and 2018 (38 C.F.R. § 4.118)
what_this_means: VA's rules for rating skin scars and facial/neck disfigurement (Diagnostic Codes 7800–7805) changed substantially across four eras. Before August 30, 2002, head, face, and neck scars used broad descriptive terms. On August 30, 2002, VA introduced an 8-item checklist of measurable disfigurement features (up to 80%). On October 23, 2008, VA switched painful or unstable scars (Diagnostic Code 7804) from a flat 10% cap to a scar-count scale (10% for 1–2 scars, 20% for 3–4 scars, 30% for 5 or more scars, plus 10% if both painful and unstable). On August 13, 2018, VA removed the 'nonlinear' shape restriction on deep scars and defined six body zones.
record_clues: C&P scar examination worksheets listing multiple tender, painful, or repeatedly breaking-down surgical or shrapnel scars.
Head, face, or neck scars measuring 5+ inches long or 1/4+ inch wide, or showing sunken/raised contour, skin adherence, color changes, or tissue loss.
Deep burn or shrapnel scars on the trunk, arms, or legs covering 6 square inches or more with underlying soft-tissue damage.
important_cautions: Do not apply post-October 23, 2008 scar-counting percentages (20% or 30% under Diagnostic Code 7804) as a Clear and Unmistakable Error (CUE) argument against a decision issued before October 23, 2008, when the regulation capped superficial painful scars at 10%.

Proposed / Not Enacted Alert: On September 29, 2025 (90 FR 46542), VA published a proposed, unfinalized rule regarding objective pain confirmation under Diagnostic Code 7804. Because 90 FR 46542 is proposed and not enacted law, current enacted § 4.118 standards remain in effect.
A painful or disfiguring scar rating can often exist alongside a separate rating for underlying muscle, nerve, or joint damage when distinct symptoms are involved.
questions_for_representative: Were my painful or unstable scars evaluated before or after October 23, 2008, and does my current rating reflect the total count of painful or unstable scars?
For head, face, or neck scars, did the examiner measure all eight objective disfigurement characteristics under Diagnostic Code 7800?
Are there underlying muscle, nerve, or range-of-motion limitations caused by the injury that should be evaluated separately under Diagnostic Code 7805?
